metadata.worksheet_line_p2_maximum_allowable_dedu: Page 2, "Worksheet for Pension Income Deduction - Schedule 1S, Line 4", line P2 "Maximum allowable deduction" prints 48,216.00 in both the Taxpayer and Spouse columns. Line P1 is total eligible non-military pension income (both Maine and non-Maine sources) included in federal adjusted gross income (from federal Form 1040, lines 4b and 5b or Form 1040-SR, lines 4b and 5b); line P3 is total social security and railroad retirement benefits received, whether taxable or not; line P4 subtracts P3 from P2 (if zero or less, enter zero); line P5 is the smaller of P1 or P4; line P9 is total eligible military retirement pay included in federal adjusted gross income; line P10 adds P8 and P9.
metadata.worksheet_phaseout_caution: The worksheet's CAUTION states that if Form 1040ME, line 14 is more than $125,000 if single or married filing separately, $187,500 if head of household, or $250,000 if married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse, the Worksheet for Phaseout of Non-Military Pension Income Deduction must be completed.

metadata.conformity_cover_page_note: Page 1 is an MRS "IMPORTANT UPDATE" cover page stating that Maine conforms to the Internal Revenue Code as of December 31, 2024, that federal Public Law 119-21 changes are expected to be considered in the Second Regular Session of the 132nd Maine Legislature, and that the 2025 returns and instructions were developed under the Governor's directive pending conformity legislation.
metadata.line_4_pension_income_deduction: Page 8, Schedule 1S line 4 instructions: "Enter the pension income deduction from the Pension Income Deduction Worksheet, line P10. Include copies of your 1099 forms to verify the subtraction. Enclose worksheet. 36 M.R.S. § 5122(2)(M-2)." The instructions state that you and your spouse (if married) may each deduct up to $48,216 of other eligible pension income that is included in federal adjusted gross income, and that "The $48,216 cap must be reduced by any social security and railroad retirement benefits received, whether taxable or not." Benefits received under a United States military retirement plan, including survivor benefits, are stated to be fully exempt.
